To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Cycles of 2-day fasting in mice reduced autoimmune disease and increased lymphocyte-dependent killing of cancer cells.

(1) fasting induces a metabolic switch in CD8 T cells from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis; (2) this metabolic switch is mediated by a decrease in the expression of the mitochondrial pyruvate transporter MCT1; (3) this metabolic switch results in a decrease in the mitochondrial mass and function in CD8 T cells; and (4) this decrease in mitochondrial mass and function is mediated by the proteasome.
fasting and calorie restriction (CR) have a strong impact on the immune system, and the mechanisms responsible are not yet fully understood.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the immune system in health and disease and with the study of immunological aspects of cancer, with the ultimate objective to improve the diagnosis, prognosis and treatment of cancer and autoimmune diseases.
understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the regulation of immune responses.

the following questions: What are the effects of fasting on immune cells, and how do these effects change during fasting and refeeding? What are the mechanisms by which fasting affects immune cells? How do these mechanisms relate to the anti-tumor and anti-inflammatory effects of fasting?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fasting is good for the immune system, but the mechanisms and consequences are complex and not completely understood.
fasting and severe calorie deprivation are powerful tools to activate the immune system and reduce autoimmunity.
fasting induces an anti-cancer immune surveillance and anti-inflammatory response by activating a complex interplay between the immune system and the metabolic pathways of the host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cycles of fasting induce a profound change in immune cell composition and function in the bone marrow, thymus, spleen, and peripheral lymph nodes, and that these changes are driven by a decrease in the availability of amino acids and glucose.
fasting induces a complex reorganization of the immune system that shifts it from a pro-inflammatory state to an anti-inflammatory one and that is mediated by epigenetic and metabolic mechanisms.
fasting is a powerful anti-cancer therapy that can be used as an adjunct to conventional therapies to improve the efficacy of cancer treatments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fasting and calorie restriction are powerful regulators of the immune system that can be harnessed to fight cancer and autoimmune diseases.
fasting induces a metabolic state that is similar to cancer cells in the tumor microenvironment and that this state is required for the anti-tumor effects of fasting.
fasting induces a profound change in the composition of immune cells in the blood and tissues, and these changes are mediated by a variety of mechanisms.
